title: R14a: jev_route active ranking (Phase I P5) — bounded Jev suitability adjustment over empirical scores, cold-start and failure reproduce baseline, plus the missing routing tests
spec:
Why: [jev.routing].mode accepts "active" but jev_route.shadow_context (orchestrator/jev_route.py:165-176) only emits a notify() stub ("active ranking lands in P5"); hypothetical() (146-163) is the shadow heuristic. Phase I P5 requires active mode to modify ranking among eligible candidates as candidate_score = configured_weight x empirical_score x jev_suitability_adjustment, with extreme probabilities unable to overwhelm strong empirical evidence, cold start safe, failure reproducing baseline. The audit (T-0573) also found shadow-isolation and active-mode untested.
What (orchestrator/jev_route.py and tests/test_jev_route.py only; the executor.start hook that passes the adjusted scores into pool.pick_executor is a separate integration task):
- adjustment(signals, evidence, eligible_ids, cfg) -> {executor_id: multiplier in [1 - max_adjustment, 1 + max_adjustment]} with cfg [jev.routing] max_adjustment (default 0.25), evidence_floor_n (default 10): direction from the same signals hypothetical() uses (substantial_reasoning/architectural/stronger_executor_helps favour higher class_success; localized_simple with low elevated_risk favours lower expected_cost); magnitude scaled by Jev confidence and shrunk toward 1.0 by a factor n/(n+evidence_floor_n) where n is the executor's sample count, so strong empirical evidence bounds the effect; missing signals or evidence -> 1.0 for every executor (cold start).
- active_scores(task, pool, eligible, classification, evidence, base_scores=None) -> {executor_id: base_score x multiplier} for mode active only; any failure (classification None, malformed signals, empty eligible) returns base_scores unchanged (baseline reproduced); shadow and off return base_scores unchanged; never introduces ids outside eligible.
- shadow_context() keeps its shape and adds "adjustment" (computed in shadow and active for telemetry) and "active": bool; drop the notify stub; record_shadow logs adjustment and mode.
- Config documentation in the module docstring; no pool.toml edit (defaults in code).
Tests to add (unittest.TestCase): active can change ranking; shadow never changes routing; extreme probability cannot overturn strong evidence; cold start yields multipliers 1.0; classification failure reproduces base scores; multiplier bounds respected; cooldown/eligibility never bypassed (an executor missing from eligible never gains a score).
acceptance: tests/test_jev_route.py::test_active_mode_adjusts_ranking_within_bounds — mode active, signals favouring a stronger executor with confidence 0.9 and n 3 yield multipliers within [0.75, 1.25] and the favoured executor's score rises relative to the other
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_shadow_mode_never_changes_scores — mode shadow returns base_scores unchanged while shadow_context still reports the adjustment
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_extreme_probability_cannot_overturn_strong_evidence — signal 1.0 against an executor with n 200 and class_success 0.95 leaves that executor ranked first
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_cold_start_and_failure_reproduce_baseline — no evidence yields every multiplier 1.0; classification None in active mode returns base_scores identical to the input
tests/test_jev_route.py::test_active_scores_never_add_ineligible_executor — an executor absent from eligible receives no score even when signals favour it

constraints.interface_contract: adjustment(signals, evidence, eligible_ids, cfg) -> {id: multiplier}; active_scores(task, pool, eligible, classification, evidence, base_scores=None) -> {id: score}; shadow_context() gains keys adjustment and active; config [jev.routing] max_adjustment 0.25, evidence_floor_n 10 defaulted in code; existing functions classify, hypothetical, record_shadow keep their signatures

result.summary: superseded by R14a v2 T-0602 after spec review T-0590 request_changes (per-class sample count via scorecard.class_sample_size, base_scores default defined)

spec_review_risks.issue: adjustment()'s shrinkage factor n/(n+evidence_floor_n) requires a per-executor, per-class sample count n, but no in-scope function returns one. scorecard.class_success() (scorecard.py:64-91) computes this exact count internally as len(resolved) but only returns the success ratio, discarding n. The only per-executor count reachable from evidence_for() (jev_route.py:135-143) is scorecard.executor_economics()'s n_tasks, which aggregates lineage-root tasks across ALL task classes for that executor, not the class-conditioned n the shrinkage math assumes. Using n_tasks would let an executor's unrelated experience in other classes suppress shrinkage for a class it has barely touched (e.g. 3 samples at min_samples for 'architectural' but 200 total tasks overall), which is the opposite of what evidence_floor_n is meant to guard against. Scope forbids touching scorecard.py, and the spec's 'What' section doesn't direct evidence_for() to compute or source a real per-class n.

active_scores(task, pool, eligible, classification, evidence, base_scores=None) leaves the base_scores=None default undefined on the non-failure path (mode active, valid classification): should base_score default to 1.0 per eligible executor, or is the caller always expected to supply real scores? None of the five acceptance tests exercise the default-None success path, so this is a real ambiguity an implementer will resolve arbitrarily.
